skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Creates detailed, test-driven implementation plans from specifications or requirements before coding begins.
skill.summary: Turn software requirements into precise, executable implementation plans.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 16 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, file paths, and benign development command examples. No executable scripts, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious command behavior was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 uses Markdown inline code to show a plan file path. It does not execute Ruby, shell, or any external command.
Lines 33 through 45 are a fenced Markdown example for a plan document header. The backticks only delimit documentation content.
Line 45 closes a Markdown code fence. It contains no command invocation or executable expression.
Line 49 opens a fenced Markdown example that demonstrates plan formatting. It does not invoke a shell.
Line 53 presents a placeholder file path using Markdown inline code. No dynamic input or execution mechanism is present.
Line 54 presents a placeholder source path and line range. The backticks are documentation formatting only.
Line 55 formats a placeholder test path as inline code. It does not run the test or construct a command.
Line 59 opens a Python example fence within the plan template. Markdown fencing is not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 63 closes a Python example fence. It has no executable command behavior.
Line 67 shows a fixed pytest command that an implementation plan may recommend. It is documentation and is not executed by this skill.
Line 72 opens another Python example fence. It only demonstrates the expected structure of a written plan.
Line 75 closes a Python example fence. No shell expansion or command execution occurs.
Line 79 repeats a fixed pytest verification command as plan documentation. The skill does not execute it or accept command input.
Lines 84 through 87 contain benign git commands inside a Bash example fence. They are illustrative plan content without an execution mechanism.
Line 87 closes the Bash example fence. The delimiter itself cannot invoke an external command.
Line 88 closes the surrounding Markdown template fence. It is formatting syntax, not shell backtick execution.

content.value_statement: Complex software requirements can produce vague tasks, missed tests, and costly rework. This skill creates precise, test-driven plans with files, commands, and checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Converts a feature specification into ordered, bite-sized implementation tasks.
Identifies exact files to create, modify, and test for each task.
Defines failing tests before minimal implementation steps.
Includes verification commands and expected results.
Adds architecture, technology, and goal summaries to each plan.
Provides commit checkpoints and execution handoff options.
limitations: Requires a clear specification or requirements before planning.
Cannot verify file paths or architecture without access to the target repository.
Produces plans but does not implement the planned changes.
Assumes the project supports tests and version control.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Break a product requirement into tested coding tasks with exact files and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Work for a Team
use_cases.description: Create a shared implementation sequence that reduces ambiguity during assignment and review.

use_cases.title: Translate Requirements into Tasks
use_cases.description: Convert accepted requirements into a practical plan before development begins.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [feature]. Use these requirements: [requirements]. Include tasks, files, tests, and verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when requirements are short and the repository structure is known.

prompt_templates.title: Plan from a Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this specification: [specification]. Create a test-driven implementation plan with exact file paths, small steps, expected results, and commit checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a detailed feature specification is available.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-System Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this change across [systems]. Address interfaces, migrations, compatibility, tests, documentation, rollout, and rollback. Identify dependencies and verification commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes that affect several services or application layers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan with Risk Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [complex change]. Include assumptions, alternatives, security risks, failure cases, observability, staged rollout, rollback, and acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced work with operational or security impact.

output_examples.input: Plan an email verification feature for a web application.
output: Goal: Add secure email verification for new accounts.
Task 1: Add token persistence and expiration tests.
Task 2: Implement token creation and validation.
Task 3: Add the verification endpoint and user interface.
Task 4: Run focused tests, then run the full suite.

output_examples.input: Plan a database migration that adds order status history.
output: Architecture: Store immutable status events linked to each order.
Task 1: Add migration tests and define rollback behavior.
Task 2: Create the history table and indexes.
Task 3: Update write paths and backfill existing orders.
Task 4: Verify metrics, compatibility, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Provide the specification, repository structure, and relevant technical constraints.
Review every proposed file path and command before implementation.
Keep each task small enough to test and review independently.
anti_patterns: Do not request a plan without clear requirements or acceptance criteria.
Do not accept placeholders when exact files and tests can be identified.
Do not combine unrelated changes into one large implementation task.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: No. It creates an implementation plan that another session or developer can execute.

faq.question: What input produces the best plan?
faq.answer: Provide requirements, acceptance criteria, repository context, constraints, and relevant file paths.

faq.question: Does the plan include tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow places failing tests before minimal implementation and includes verification steps.

faq.question: Can it plan changes across several services?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide each service boundary, interface, dependency, and deployment constraint.

faq.question: Will every suggested command work unchanged?
faq.answer: Not always. Verify commands against the project tooling and local environment before execution.

faq.question: Where does the skill suggest saving plans?
faq.answer: It suggests the docs/plans directory with a date and feature name in the filename.
